body.p: Reconsideration of the Application is respectfully requested. No new matter has been added.
I. Status of the Claims

Claims 24-27, 29-34, and 36-44 are pending in the application with Claims 24 and 37 amended; Claims 1-23, 28, and 35 cancelled herein; and Claims 25-27, 29-34, 36, and 38-44 remaining as previously presented. No new matter is believed introduced by this Response as the amendments are fully supported by the Specification and figures as originally submitted. Applicant submits that the pending claims are in condition for allowance and believes that the Application is allowable for at least the following reasons.
II. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103

The Office Action at pg. 4 rejects Claims 24-27, 32-34, 36, 38, 41, and 44 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Ruppersberg (US 2017/0065198) ("Ruppersberg") in view of Ghorraani (US 2018/0325418) ("Ghorraani"). The Office Action at pg. 6 rejects Claims 29-30, 39-40, 41-42, and 43-44 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Ruppersberg and Ghorraani, and further in view of Urman (US 2016/0038047) ("Urman")

Applicant respectfully disagrees. Nevertheless, without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103 and solely to expedite prosecution, Applicant has amended Claim 1 to clarify further patentably-distinguishing elements of the disclosed technology. Applicant respectfully submits that the references of record do not show, disclose, or suggest at least:
receive a first signal indicative of electrical activity in myocardial tissue,
the first signal being received from the plurality of electrodes of the expandable
basket assembly;
receive a second signal indicative of a respective position of the plurality
of electrodes of the expandable basket assembly;
determine a geometric center of the plurality of electrodes of the
expandable basket assembly;
as recited in Claim 24. In contrast, although Ruppersberg arguably discloses an expandable basket assembly, Ruppersberg fails to disclose receiving a first signal from the plurality of

electrodes, a second signal indicative of a position of the plurality of electrodes, and determining a geometric center of the plurality of electrodes (the foregoing was conceded in the Office Action at pg. 4). Accordingly, Ruppersberg fails to disclose an "expandable basket catheter" and system that can receive a first signal from the plurality of electrodes, receive a second signal indicative of a position of the plurality of electrodes, and determine a geometric center of the plurality of electrodes as required by Claim 24.

To cure the deficiencies of Ruppersberg, the Office relies upon Ghorraani. Ghorraani, however, fails to cure the deficiencies of Ruppersberg. Instead, Ghorraani discloses "a means to guide the placement of an MPDC in the atria to locate the AF sources (rotors and foci)," (Ghorraani at [0066], MPDC meaning a "Multi-Pole Diagnostic Catheter") wherein, "guidance of MPDC placement is provided by the present solution via an AF ablation target map." (Ghorraani at [0066]). The "multi-polar catheter" as disclosed in Ghorraani at [0028] is not the same as the basket catheter recited in Claim 24. Rather, Ghorraani discourages use of a basket catheter and emphasizes the "limitations of the basket catheter" (Ghorraani at 0003). Specifically, Ghorraani states:

"Moreover, regions such as the left SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.6932.417 covered by the basket catheter. As a result,
arrhythmia substrates involving these struct
mapping does not permit immediate correl
anatomical sites." (Ghorraani at 0003, emphasis added).

Applicant submits that Ghorraani discourages against the use of a basket catheter as recited in Claim 24 and cannot be combined to arrive at the claimed invention. Therefore, although Ruppersberg discloses the use of an expandable basket assembly, it would not have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the disclosure of Ruppersberg with the disclosure of Ghorraani to arrive at the claimed invention. That is, there is no motivation or suggestion to combine and, therefore, no prima facie obviousness can be established. Accordingly, Ghorraani, alone or in combination with Ruppersberg, fails to show, disclose, or suggest all of the features recited in Claim 24 and Claim 24 is allowable over Ghorraani.
Urman fails to cure the deficiencies of Ruppersberg and Ghorraani. Instead, Urman
discloses "Typically, probe 24 comprises a catheter which is inserted into the body of a human

subject 26 during a mapping procedure performed by a user 28 of system 20" Urman at [0033]. However, Urman is silent regarding the specificity of the type of catheter utilized and is all together silent regarding the use of an expandable basket assembly. Therefore, Urman, alone or in combination with Ruppersberg or Ghorraani, fails to show, disclose, or suggest all of the features recited in Claim 24 and Claim 24 is therefore allowable over Urman.

Where all claimed features are not shown or described in the relied upon prior art, Office personnel (as noted in MPEP § 2141) must explain why the differences between the relied-upon prior art and the claimed invention would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art.

For at least the foregoing reasons, the references of record fail to show, disclose, or suggest each of the features of Claim 24 and Claim 24 is therefore allowable over the references of record. Claim 37 has been similarly amended and are allowable for similar reasons. Further, all claims depending from Claims 24 and 37 are allowable at least by virtue of their dependency on an allowable base claim and for further features recited herein. Accordingly, Applicant requests withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103 and the claims be allowed.

It is believed the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is respectfully requested to contact the undersigned if there are any remaining issues which can be resolved by a Supplemental or Examiner's Amendment.
